walkthroughs.body_html:
In chemistry, pure means a single element or compound — nothing else.

A pure substance melts and boils at a sharp, exact temperature. A mixture melts over a range. Bottled water is a mixture; pure H2O is the chemist's meaning of pure.

A formulation is a mixture designed to do a job, with each ingredient in a measured amount.

Examples: paints, fuels, cleaning products, fertilisers, alloys, medicines. The recipe matters — change a quantity and it stops working as intended.

Draw the baseline in pencil (ink would run). Add small spots of each sample on the baseline.

Stand the paper in solvent so the level is below the baseline — otherwise the spots dissolve into the solvent pool. The solvent (mobile phase) rises through the paper (stationary phase) and separates the dyes.

mcqs.q: Why is the chromatography baseline drawn in pencil?
options: Pencil is easier to see
Ink would dissolve and run up the paper
Pencil reacts with the solvent
Ink is too expensive

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
Water is bent because oxygen is heavier than hydrogen and weighs the middle down.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.

mcqs.q: Why does water have a bent shape rather than linear?
options: Oxygen has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, giving a tetrahedral electron geometry but a bent molecular shape.
A buffer destroys added acid by changing it into water vapour.
Water is bent because oxygen is heavier than hydrogen and weighs the middle down.
Water is bent because the hydrogens repel each other and push apart.

mcqs.q: How does a buffer maintain its pH when small amounts of acid are added?
options: Water is bent because oxygen is heavier than hydrogen and weighs the middle down.
The conjugate base in the buffer reacts with added H+ to remove it, keeping pH nearly constant.
A buffer prevents any H+ ions from being added to the solution at all.
A buffer destroys added acid by changing it into water vapour.
